known_facts_book1: The big, powerful, black-bearded King of the Island of Regos, at war with all the rest of the world.
Sends raiding parties to conquer and pillage neighboring islands, and his slaves — captured in many countries — work his gold and silver mines under cruel overseers with whips.
Orders the palace of Pingaree torn down so that not one stone remains upon another, and every house on the island destroyed.
Does not believe in magic and calls Buzzub a coward and a weakling for reporting it — then flees his own city when Inga bursts the gates.
Is a coward at heart, like all bullies and marauders, and abandons Regos entirely rather than face the boy.
Is taunted by his own wife for being driven out by a boy, a roly-poly King and a billy goat.
Fetches King Kitticut from the mines the night before Inga arrives, at Queen Cor's suggestion, so the parents can be used as hostages.
Carries both royal prisoners to the Nome King and buys their keeping with bags of gold and jewels the prisoners themselves are forced to carry.
Tells Kaliko an elaborate lie — that the King and Queen of Pingaree are evil invaders and their son a terrible wizard — which Kaliko recognizes as a lie and accepts anyway.
Is drowned with Queen Cor in a storm at sea on the way back to Regos, which Dorothy reads in Glinda's Record Book; neither is ever seen again in the book after the caverns.

known_relations_book1.Queen Cor: His wife and fellow ruler, drowned with him.
known_relations_book1.Inga: The boy Prince who takes his city without a blow.
known_relations_book1.King Kitticut: The King he enslaves, then sells to the nomes.
known_relations_book1.Kaliko: The Nome King he bribes to keep his prisoners.
known_relations_book1.Buzzub: His big captain, whom he calls a coward.

not_in_this_book: King Gos is killed by Inga
relationships: King Gos is an ally of Inga
King Gos is a friend of Kitticut

known_facts_book1: Queen of the Island of Coregos, wedded to King Gos, and so stern and cruel that her people cannot decide which of their sovereigns they dread most.
A big woman almost as tall as Gos, with flashing black eyes and a dark complexion, whose evil expression she tries to cover by smiling sweetly when she means the most mischief.
Rules the grain fields of Coregos with slaves who are mostly women, and puts Queen Garee in the royal dairy to make butter.
Is fond of honey and buys it once a year from Zella, the charcoal-burner's daughter.
Calls her husband a coward and says no magic can stand against a woman's cunning.
Captures Inga by walking up to him under pretence of an invitation and throwing both long arms around him in a grip like a vise, then kicking Rinkitink in the stomach and calling for ropes.
Makes Inga her page and threatens to use Rinkitink as a pincushion and to tickle the soles of his feet with a feather.
Slaps Inga twice for brushing her ear with a peacock-feather fan, and sends for the whip with the seven lashes to beat the women of Pingaree.
Learns the magic is real only when her dagger rebounds from Inga's breast, by which time she has already lost.
Drags Queen Garee out of the butter-house and across the bridge of boats in her flight, and conceives the whole hostage plot that sends the prisoners to the nomes.
Is drowned with King Gos in a storm at sea, as Dorothy reads in Glinda's Record Book.

known_relations_book1.King Gos: Her husband, whom she taunts as a coward and drowns beside.
known_relations_book1.Inga: The boy she captures with her own arms and makes her page.
known_relations_book1.Queen Garee: Her dairy slave, dragged away as a hostage.
known_relations_book1.Rinkitink: The King she threatens to use as a pincushion.
known_relations_book1.Zella: The girl who brings her honey each year.

not_in_this_book: Queen Cor is killed by Inga
Queen Cor buys Zella's honey in this book
relationships: Queen Cor is a friend of Zella
Queen Cor is an ally of Inga

known_facts_book1: The big captain who leads the warriors of Regos down to the shore to meet Inga's boat.
Jeers at the 'baby Prince' and says Rinkitink will make a fine slave for Queen Cor, who loves to tickle fat men and see them jump.
Orders two flights of arrows and spears at the three strangers, all of which bound harmlessly back.
Is caught by Bilbil's charge, sprawls headlong, rolls over two or three times and runs yelling after his own fleeing men.
Reports the magic to King Gos and is called a coward and a weakling for it.
Tells Inga, on his return from the mines, that the King and Queen have run away with forty rowers and taken the King and Queen of Pingaree with them.
Is given command of the warriors by Inga and made to promise to keep his men quiet and orderly — if he can.

known_relations_book1.King Gos: His King, who scorns his report of magic.
known_relations_book1.Inga: The boy who first routs him and later puts him in command.
known_relations_book1.Bilbil: The goat that knocks him sprawling.
